report:
## Verdict: REJECT (four verification-checklist FAILs stand after normalization; the headline defect is a diff-added test comment that misstates this PR's own pre-fix behaviour, corroborated 4/4)

## Issue Compliance
Reviewed against issue #1915: Credential scrub eats the JSON escape backslash after a redacted token - criteria from workpad; scope unchanged. Requirement-based checklist items are included in the verification results below.
Criteria came from the `/prflow:implement` workpad comment - this run's authoritative set, possibly narrowed from the issue.
No divergence between the workpad's criteria and the issue body's.

The core fix is correct and was verified by execution, not by reading. Against `origin/main` the round-trip fixture produces unparseable JSON (the lone `\` of a `\"` is eaten, ending the string early); against HEAD it re-parses. That is the #1915 bug, and it is genuinely pinned.

## Verification Checklist Results
14 passed, 4 failed, 0 inconclusive - 0 via lite probe, 18 via agent.
- VC-4: FAIL - the four-shape JSON round-trip test is not inside the `#1064 D4` sub-block the criterion names; it sits under its own `#1915` header in the broader `#1064` section [lib/test/run.sh]
- VC-11: FAIL - `{4,}` does not block recorded-command corruption generally; `sed 's/AUTHORIZATION: basic //gI'` and `////` are still rewritten [scripts/scrub-credentials.sh]
- VC-12: FAIL - a credential containing a lone backslash followed by an ordinary character was fully redacted pre-fix and is now truncated, leaving a live tail [.changeset/issue-1915-scrub-escape-backslash.md]
- VC-14: FAIL - the four escape-unit assertions are non-discriminating for this change; measured pre-fix output is full redaction, not truncation [lib/test/run.sh]

<details><summary>Passed items (14 of 18) - click to expand</summary>

- VC-1: basic credential inside a JSON string still parses after scrubbing
- VC-2: same for the Bearer rule with a non-GitHub token
- VC-3: a recorded `sed 's/AUTHORIZATION: basic //'` keeps its trailing slashes
- VC-5: all four shapes still redacted; no assertion weakened or deleted
- VC-6: the four-backslash alternative matches exactly two backslash bytes, not a lone one
- VC-7: BSD/macOS `sed -E` accepts the interval quantifier on the alternation group
- VC-8: the `#` delimiter introduces no stray-delimiter hazard
- VC-9: the trailing hyphen in the class is literal
- VC-10: a lone backslash before a closing quote survives at every backslash-run length 1-6
- VC-13: `$SCR` and `$DEN_JQ` are bound before the new block and never reassigned
- VC-15: each fixture reaches the scrubber as the byte sequence its label names
- VC-16: the coverage-map `1915` entry matches its neighbours and sorts correctly
- VC-17: every added comment run is within the three-line cap and prevention-shaped
- VC-18: the changeset frontmatter matches the consolidator's expected keys and vocabulary

</details>

## Code Review Findings

### Important / Major
1. The `{4,}` floor is pinned for the `basic` rule only - the `Bearer` rule's floor is entirely unguarded. All three floor-related assertions use `AUTHORIZATION: basic`. Mutation evidence: narrowing only the `Bearer` rule's `{4,}` back to `+` leaves every new assertion green, while `run: sed 's/Authorization: Bearer //' file` regresses to the recorded-command corruption this PR exists to fix; the symmetric below-floor leak of a 1-3 unit Bearer credential is unpinned in the other direction. The two rules are a hand-maintained coupled mirror and the PR's own comment binds both. (raised by 1/4 agents) [suspected over-grade: shape 3 - uncorroborated single-source from pr-test-analyzer; annotation only, severity unchanged]

### Suggestion / Minor
1. The comment above the escape-unit assertions claims "the pre-fix behaviour is that truncation, not a whole no-match". That is false against `origin/main`: inside a POSIX ERE bracket expression a backslash is a literal member, so the old class already contained `\` and matched both fixtures end-to-end - measured pre-fix output is full redaction. All four escape assertions pass unmodified against the pre-fix script, so they are forward guards against a later narrowing, not RED-first witnesses for this change. Reword the clause to name the narrowing as the counterfactual rather than this PR's predecessor. (raised by 4/4 agents)
2. Both rewritten rules match the auth *scheme* keyword case-sensitively past its first letter (`[Bb]earer` / `[Bb]asic`), while the header *name* uses per-letter classes. `AUTHORIZATION: BASIC AAAABBBBCCCC` passes through verbatim - the whole credential reaches the published transcript with exit 0 and no warning. HTTP auth schemes are case-insensitive per RFC 7235. Pre-existing, but both lines were rewritten wholesale here and the fix is one class each. This is a fail-open, so it is not eligible for the shape-1 over-grade annotation. (raised by 1/4 agents)
3. The changeset's "the header keyword itself is rewritten to its canonical casing" is ambiguous: group 1 captures and preserves the header *name* verbatim (`authorization:` stays lowercase); what the replacement canonicalises is the auth *scheme* keyword. One agent read the clause as false and another verified it as true, so the truthfulness sweep does not promote it - it is reworded for clarity, not filed as a falsehood. (raised by 1/4 agents)
4. The changeset's "The four redacted shapes are unchanged" sits in tension with VC-12's measured narrowing (a token containing a lone backslash before an ordinary character now truncates). Since no member of the four credential alphabets contains a raw backslash, the claim is not demonstrated false within its own scope and is not routed into the self-contradicting-diff carve-out; disclosing the escape-unit narrowing alongside the four-unit floor would close the gap. (raised by 1/4 agents)

- No Phase-3 finding reaches the resolved `verdict_severity_threshold` of `critical`.
- The Phase 4.1.5 behavior-inert prose cap covers Suggestion 1: limb one holds (no tool parses that comment to decide behavior - the repo's declaration-marker set does not include it and no reader was found), and limb two holds (`.github/actions/vendor-plugin/vendor-slice.sh` prunes `lib/test` from the consumer slice, so it ships to nobody). Its subject is the sentence, not the assertions' coverage - the assertions remain valid forward guards either way - so it is capped at Suggestion and drives no REJECT.
- No deferral block in the PR body, so Phase 4.0 demoted nothing and the Deferrals section is omitted.
- The Phase 3.1 dirty-tree backstop compared clean (cmp rc=0): no review agent mutated the working tree.
